_readme: Fill this file in and the page is done — nothing in index.html or scripts/ should need editing. Anything set to null disappears from the page. Run `node scripts/validate-config.js` when you are finished. See SETUP.md.

page.title: Regional parliament election in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern · 2026
page._postUrlComment: The WordPress post this page is embedded in. Used by scripts/check-embed.js, which is the only thing that looks at it — the page never calls back to the post. Set it once the post exists.
page._pagesUrlComment: Where this page is published. Publish it alongside the article: it is served from a CDN and executes no PHP, so it stays up when the WordPress host does not.
page.citation: Europe Elects. (2026, September 19). Germany: Regional parliament election in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2026. Europe Elects.
page.sources: Infratest dimap (ARD), Forschungsgruppe Wahlen (ZDF), INSA, Forsa, pollytix, Landeswahlleiter Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

election.title: Regional parliament election in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern

jurisdiction._comment: `territory` is the sub-national unit for a regional election. `territoryNative` is the local-language spelling; here it is the same either way.

election._firstProjectionComment: ARD and ZDF publish an exit-poll Prognose the moment polls close at 18:00 and the first full Hochrechnung about a quarter of an hour later.
election._seatsFixedComment: false: the Landtag has 71 statutory seats but overhang and levelling seats float the total upward — it sat at 79 after 2021. That lifts the ceiling on a seat projection rather than dropping the check.
election._seatsTotalComment: Statutory size: 36 constituency seats plus 35 list seats. Used to sanity-check seat figures coming out of the Sheet, with seatsFixed false widening the band.
election._ballotNameComment: Voters cast an Erststimme for a constituency candidate and a Zweitstimme for a state list. The Zweitstimme decides the seat distribution and is what this page reports.

previous.note: 79 seats including overhang and levelling seats
previous._comment: The election this one is compared against. Held the same day as the 2021 federal election, which is part of why turnout was high.

sheet._idComment: Must be shared as Anyone with the link → Viewer. Both the Action and the browser read this through the gviz CSV endpoint with no credentials at all, so a restricted Sheet returns HTTP 401 to everything — the pipeline, the page's fallback read, and Datawrapper's linked dataset alike.
sheet._tabsComment: Tabs are referenced by NAME, never by gid. A gid is regenerated every time a Sheet is duplicated; the name survives. These names are the ones that carry over from the Saxony-Anhalt Sheet — check them against the tab strip after copying.

tabs._demographicComment: Unhooked on election day. The tab still holds the Saxony-Anhalt series the Sheet was copied from, and build-data.js fails hard on it - "unknown party DVU" / "Schill". Those are not this territory's parties, so the alternative to unhooking it was publishing another state's demographics under this heading. Point it back at the tab once a real series for this territory is typed in, and turn sections.demographics back on.

results._comment: Layout of the `results` tab. Column 0 is always the party name; these are the 0-based indexes of the rest.
results._totalRowComment: Case-insensitive regular expression matching the label of the totals row, so it is summed as an electorate figure rather than mistaken for a party. Both spellings, because the Sheet is worked on in two languages.
results._votesAreComment: The votes column holds a percentage on purpose and there is no raw vote count to report. Not the template default and not a guess: the Saxony-Anhalt Sheet these two were copied from filled that column with 17.23%, 43.80% and so on, and this Sheet's totals row already holds 0.00%. Under the count setting a percent sign marks a cell as a placeholder, so every party row would have read as not-yet-counted for the whole evening and the results table would have shown pending all night while looking perfectly healthy.
results._minValidVotesComment: Not applied while votesAre is set to share, because the guard only runs against a raw-count totals row. Kept for the day a returning officer publishes counts. Floor on the totals row. About 1.3 million people are eligible and turnout was 70.8% in 2021, so a real count clears 50,000 within the first reporting municipalities. Below it the whole tab reads as not yet counting, so a half-prepared sheet cannot put placeholder figures on the page as results.

sheet._ignoredTabsComment: Tabs the Apps Script should NOT treat as a reason to rebuild — static reference data and the team's shift roster. Keep this in step with IGNORED_TABS in Script Properties. Deliberately a deny-list: forgetting to list a tab costs one wasted no-op run, whereas an allow-list fails silently and loses data. Note that _coa_exit_ID and _coa_exit_FGW are NOT here — analysts type into them live.

source._localPathComment: Path to a local PartiesData checkout, e.g. "../PartiesData". When set it is read instead of GitHub, which is how this runs offline and without a token. Left null because the Action has no checkout to read.
source._authComment: PartiesData is a private repository, so the build reads it through the GitHub Contents API with a token from PARTIESDATA_TOKEN (a fine-grained PAT with Contents: Read on it). In the Action that is a repository secret of the same name. See SETUP.md.
source._comment: This entry is Mecklenburg-Vorpommern's own, filed under Germany as an election type, and its last_results are the 2021 state election — so it is a real baseline and nothing has to be borrowed. Run `node scripts/fetch-parties.js --list` to print what exists for a country.

parties._metadataFallbackComment: Only group, colour and full name are taken from a fallback; last_results never is, because a federal result is not a state baseline. It is here so a federal spelling appearing in the Sheet (CDU/CSU, say) still resolves.
parties._baselineSourceComment: The PartiesData entry named above is this territory's own last election, so last_results is the correct previous-result column. content/previous-result.json carries the same figures with seats, for the accordion.
parties._orderComment: Ballot order of the 19 admitted Landeslisten — the Stimmzettel ranks parties by their 2021 second-vote count — followed by the two parties that contested 2021 but are not standing again, so they sort to the bottom of the results table.

overrides._comment: Keyed by the party's key in PartiesData. Every field is optional — anything omitted is derived. `aliases` adds spellings the Sheet may use; the key, the code and the display name already match automatically.

Tierschutz.name: Tierschutzpartei
Tierschutz._colorComment: Deliberate departure: PartiesData files this party under LEFT, which would give it Die Linke's dark red. The animal-rights palette entry is both truer and legible next to it.

FW.name: FW (RE)
FW._colorComment: Deliberate departure: FW sits with Renew, which would hand it the FDP's yellow. Both are on the ballot, so one has to move.

PARTEI.name: Die PARTEI
PARTEI.full: Partei für Arbeit, Rechtsstaat, Tierschutz, Elitenförderung und basisdemokratische Initiative

Basis.name: dieBasis
Basis._comment: Contested 2021 (1.7%) and is not on the 2026 ballot. Kept so its 2021 figure has a name and a colour.

HEIMAT.name: Die Heimat
HEIMAT._comment: Contested 2021 as the NPD (0.8%) and is not on the 2026 ballot.

extra._comment: The nine smaller lists admitted for 2026 that the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern PartiesData entry does not carry, because none of them has a 2021 state result to record. `name` and `color` are required here — there is nothing upstream to derive them from. Worth adding to PartiesData proper rather than leaving here.

ÖDP.name: ÖDP
ÖDP._colorComment: Deliberate departure: its MEP sits with Greens/EFA, which would hand it the same green as Bündnis 90/Die Grünen.

KPD.name: KPD
KPD._aliasComment: KDP is a transposition of KPD and is how the party is spelled in the Sheet's results tab. Kept as an alias so a corrected Sheet and an uncorrected one both resolve — without it the row falls into Others, which on a results table looks like a real figure for a party nobody can find.

PdF.name: PdF
PdF._colorComment: PartiesData files PdF under RE elsewhere, which collides with both the FDP and FW. Teal keeps all three apart.

sections._comment: The page is built from these, in this order. Set any section to null to remove it completely. Charts are Datawrapper embeds: `id` is the 5-character chart ID, `version` the published version in the embed URL (a fresh copy starts at 1), `live: true` means the chart reads the Sheet and the Action republishes it on every update.

results.label: Results
results.heading: All contesting parties
results.sub: The 19 state lists admitted for 20 September 2026, with their European party affiliation, followed by the two parties that contested 2021 and are not standing again. Official second-vote results and the change vs. 2021 populate after polls close at 18:00 CEST.

projections.label: Projections
projections.heading: Infratest dimap & Forschungsgruppe Wahlen · projections over time
projections.sub: A mix of exit poll and counted result, published and revised by both institutes through election night
projections.note: Both institutes publish a first projection at about 18:15 CEST on 20 September 2026 and revise it as counting proceeds. These charts stay empty until then.

exitVotes.label: Exit Poll · Popular Vote
exitVotes.heading: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2026 · exit poll, popular vote
exitVotes.sub: Second-vote share by party, as published at 18:00 CEST when polls close
exitVotes.empty: Exit poll figures will appear here once published.

exitSeats.label: Exit Poll · Seats
exitSeats.heading: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2026 · exit poll, seat estimate
exitSeats.sub: Projected seats by party, as published at 18:00 CEST
exitSeats.empty: Exit poll seat estimates will appear here once published.

turnout.label: Turnout by the Hour
turnout.heading: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2026 · turnout by the hour
turnout.sub: Cumulative turnout reported through election day, local time
turnout.note: How turnout built through the day, this election against previous ones. Turnout was 70.8% in 2021, when the state election was held alongside the federal one.
turnout.empty: Turnout figures for this election are not in this chart yet. It reappears on its own once the chart is reading this election’s sheet.
turnout._emptyComment: Shown in place of the embed while the guard below fails. The check repeats on every poll, so no edit here is needed once the chart is repointed.

chart.label: Turnout
chart._requireRowsComment: A copied chart renders happily with the previous election’s figures in it and nothing outside the iframe says which dataset it holds. This asserts that the 2021 row ends on Mecklenburg-Vorpommern’s own turnout. Saxony-Anhalt, which both Sheets were copied from, shares this state’s election years exactly, so the years alone prove nothing and the value has to be checked - it reads 60.3% there. Verified against the chart’s current version, not the pinned one, because repointing and republishing is what bumps it.

previousResult.label: 2021 Result · Outgoing Landtag
previousResult.heading: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2021 · final result
previousResult.sub: 26 September 2021 · turnout 70.8% · 79 seats including overhang and levelling seats

polling.label: Pre-Election Polling
polling.heading: Voting intention since the 2021 election
polling.sub: Polls published between the two elections · second vote (Zweitstimme)
polling._yMaxComment: Top of the y-axis, in percent. Fixed so the SPD's 39.6% in 2021 and the AfD's high-thirties polling both read against the same scale.

sections._pollingHistoryComment: The long 1990-onward archive lives in the Sheet's `_pre-elex-polls` tab and has not been transcribed into content/poll-history.json yet. Set this section back to the shape in the template once it has.
sections._headToHeadComment: No published Direktwahlfrage series for Schwesig against Holm was found. Turn this section on with content/head-to-head.json once one exists — Mecklenburg-Vorpommern does not elect its minister-president directly, so it is a hypothetical question.

coalitions.label: Coalition Options
coalitions.heading: Possible coalition combinations
coalitions.sub: Combined seat share of viable coalitions, per the latest Infratest dimap and Forschungsgruppe Wahlen exit poll
coalitions.note: Coalition arithmetic appears once the first exit poll is published at 18:00 CEST on 20 September 2026. 36 of 71 seats are a majority, more where overhang and levelling seats enlarge the chamber.

sections._demographicsComment: Off: sheet.tabs.demographic is unhooked because that tab still carries the Saxony-Anhalt series. See the comment there. The section block from the template can be pasted back once this territory has its own breakdown.

history.label: Electoral History
history.heading: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern · second-vote share and seats by election, 1990–2026
history.sub: First state election after German reunification onward · the 2026 column is not a certified result until counting finishes

records._comment: Ranked comparison lists, defined in content/records.json. This section only switches them on.

automation._githubRepoComment: Used by scripts/ for log lines and by SETUP.md. The Action itself uses $GITHUB_REPOSITORY and the Apps Script reads its own GITHUB_REPO script property, so a wrong value here breaks nothing.

datawrapper._republishComment: Off. A published Datawrapper chart with a linked dataset fetches it in the reader's browser, so republishing does nothing for freshness — it mints a new version, which strands the version this config pins, and spends API quota shared across the organisation.

automation._republishUntilComment: Republishing stops this many days after election day, so a finished page cannot keep spending API quota forever.
automation._sheetFallbackComment: The page reads the generated JSON first and only falls back to reading the Sheet directly every Nth cycle — the Sheet sends no-store, so every reader hitting it goes to Google unbuffered.
